questions.prompt: Calculate (1.2 × 10⁻³) × (9.4 × 10¹). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (1.2 × 9.4) × 10^(-3 + 1); normalise to 1.128 × 10⁻¹.

questions.prompt: Calculate (1.5 × 10⁻²) ÷ (8.1 × 10²). Give your answer to 3 significant figures in standard form.
questions.solution: Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: (1.5 ÷ 8.1) × 10⁻⁴ = 0.185185… × 10⁻⁴ ≈ 1.85 × 10⁻⁵ (3 s.f.).
markPoints: A1 Correct answer in standard form to 3 significant figures

questions.prompt: Calculate (1.8 × 10⁻¹) × (7.2 × 10³). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (1.8 × 7.2) × 10^(-1 + 3); normalise to 1.296 × 10³.

questions.prompt: Calculate (2.4 × 10⁰) ÷ (6.3 × 10⁴). Give your answer to 3 significant figures in standard form.
questions.solution: Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: (2.4 ÷ 6.3) × 10⁻⁴ = 0.380952… × 10⁻⁴ ≈ 3.81 × 10⁻⁵ (3 s.f.).
markPoints: A1 Correct answer in standard form to 3 significant figures

questions.prompt: Calculate (2.7 × 10¹) × (5.4 × 10¹). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (2.7 × 5.4) × 10^(1 + 1); normalise to 1.458 × 10³.

questions.prompt: Calculate (3.2 × 10²) ÷ (4.5 × 10²). Give your answer to 3 significant figures in standard form.
questions.solution: Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: (3.2 ÷ 4.5) × 10⁰ = 0.711111… × 10⁰ ≈ 7.11 × 10⁻¹ (3 s.f.).
markPoints: A1 Correct answer in standard form to 3 significant figures

questions.prompt: Calculate (3.6 × 10³) × (3.6 × 10³). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (3.6 × 3.6) × 10^(3 + 3); normalise to 1.296 × 10⁷.

questions.prompt: Calculate (4.5 × 10⁻³) ÷ (3.2 × 10⁴). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (4.5 ÷ 3.2) × 10^(-3 − 4); normalise to 1.40625 × 10⁻⁷.

questions.prompt: Calculate (5.4 × 10⁻²) × (2.7 × 10¹). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (5.4 × 2.7) × 10^(-2 + 1); normalise to 1.458 × 10⁰.

questions.prompt: Calculate (6.3 × 10⁻¹) ÷ (2.4 × 10²). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Calculate coefficients and exponents separately: (6.3 ÷ 2.4) × 10^(-1 − 2); normalise to 2.625 × 10⁻³.

questions.prompt: Calculate 1.2 × 10⁻³ + 2.7 × 10⁻³. Give the result in standard form.
questions.solution: Exponents are equal: combine coefficients 1.2 + 2.7; normalise the answer to 3.9 × 10⁻³.
markPoints: M1 Align common powers of ten

questions.prompt: Calculate 3.2 × 10⁻² − 1.5 × 10⁻². Give the result in standard form.

questions.prompt: Calculate 1.8 × 10⁻¹ + 3.6 × 10⁻¹. Give the result in standard form.

questions.prompt: The number of grains counted by a machine is 320000. Write this count in standard form.
A counter records 3.6 × 10⁶ grains. Another records 360 000 grains. Explain which count is larger and by what factor.
questions.solution: 360 000 = 3.6 × 10⁵. The first count is larger by a factor of 10.
markPoints: M1 Express both using a common coefficient
A1 First count is 10 times the second

questions.prompt: The number of grains counted by a machine is 45000000. Write this count in standard form.
A pupil writes 540 000 000 as 54 × 10⁷. Is the value correct? Is it in standard form? Correct it if necessary.
questions.solution: The value is correct, but 54 is not between 1 inclusive and 10 exclusive. Standard form is 5.4 × 10⁸.
markPoints: B1 Correct value but invalid standard-form coefficient

questions.prompt: A sample has mass 4.5 × 10⁻⁶ g. A pupil writes 0.000045 g. Explain the error and give the correct decimal.
questions.solution: The pupil’s value is ten times too large. The correct decimal is 0.0000045 g.

questions.prompt: Two recorded values are A=5.4 × 10⁵ and B=1.2 × 10⁶. Which is larger? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: A=540000, B=1200000; therefore B is larger.

questions.prompt: Put these values in increasing order: 6.3 × 10³, 5.9 × 10⁴, 7.1 × 10². Show a comparison.
questions.solution: They are 6300, 59000 and 710. Increasing order: 7.1 × 10², 6.3 × 10³, 5.9 × 10⁴.
markPoints: M1 Valid comparison using decimals or powers

questions.prompt: Two recorded values are A=7.2 × 10⁴ and B=1.8 × 10⁵. Which is larger? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: A=72000, B=180000; therefore B is larger.

questions.prompt: A sensor records 8.1 × 10⁻⁵ m. A second reading is ten times smaller. Write the second reading in standard form.
markPoints: M1 Divide by 10 or reduce exponent by 1

questions.prompt: A rectangular card has length 1.8 × 10² mm and width 3.2 × 10¹ mm. Calculate its area in mm², giving the answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Area = length × width = (1.8 × 3.2) × 10³ = 5760 mm². In standard form this is 5.76 × 10^3 mm².
markPoints: M1 Multiply coefficients and add exponents

questions.prompt: A rectangular card has length 2.4 × 10² mm and width 3.6 × 10¹ mm. Calculate its area in mm², giving the answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Area = length × width = (2.4 × 3.6) × 10³ = 8640 mm². In standard form this is 8.64 × 10^3 mm².
markPoints: M1 Multiply coefficients and add exponents

questions.prompt: A rectangular card has length 2.7 × 10² mm and width 4.5 × 10¹ mm. Calculate its area in mm², giving the answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Area = length × width = (2.7 × 4.5) × 10³ = 12150 mm². In standard form this is 1.215 × 10^4 mm².
markPoints: M1 Multiply coefficients and add exponents

questions.prompt: A rectangular card has length 3.2 × 10² mm and width 5.4 × 10¹ mm. Calculate its area in mm², giving the answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Area = length × width = (3.2 × 5.4) × 10³ = 17280 mm². In standard form this is 1.728 × 10^4 mm².
markPoints: M1 Multiply coefficients and add exponents

questions.prompt: Two measurements are 2.7 × 10⁻³ m and 4.5 × 10⁻² m. Find their sum in standard form. Show how you align the powers.
questions.solution: Rewrite the first quantity using 10^-2: 0.27×10^-2; add to 4.5×10^-2. Answer: 4.77 × 10⁻² m.
markPoints: M1 Convert to a common exponent

questions.prompt: A cable of length 5.4 × 10⁻² m is cut into pieces each 3.0 × 10⁻³ m long, with no waste. How many pieces are made?
markPoints: M1 Divide total length by one piece length
M1 Correct coefficient and exponent operations

questions.prompt: Two measurements are 3.6 × 10⁻³ m and 6.3 × 10⁻² m. Find their sum in standard form. Show how you align the powers.
questions.solution: Rewrite the first quantity using 10^-2: 0.36×10^-2; add to 6.3×10^-2. Answer: 6.66 × 10⁻² m.
markPoints: M1 Convert to a common exponent

questions.prompt: A machine processes 2.5 × 10⁴ records per second. How many seconds are needed for 7.5 × 10⁶ records? Give the answer in standard form.
questions.solution: Time = records ÷ rate = (7.5 ÷ 2.5) × 10^(6 − 4) = 3 × 10² seconds.
markPoints: M1 Divide coefficients and subtract powers

questions.prompt: A student says “63 × 10⁸ is already standard form”. Explain the mistake and rewrite this value correctly.
questions.solution: The coefficient 63 is not in [1,10), so 63 × 10⁸ is not standard form. It equals 6.3 × 10⁹.
markPoints: B1 State coefficient must be 1 ≤ a < 10
M1 Shift coefficient one decimal place

questions.prompt: A pupil writes (3 × 10⁴) + (2 × 10³) = 5 × 10⁷. Explain the error and calculate the correct sum.
questions.solution: Exponents are not added when adding numbers. Rewrite 2 × 10³ as 0.2 × 10⁴; the sum is 3.2 × 10⁴.
markPoints: B1 Explain misuse of the multiplication rule

questions.prompt: A student says “81 × 10⁷ is already standard form”. Explain the mistake and rewrite this value correctly.
questions.solution: The coefficient 81 is not in [1,10), so 81 × 10⁷ is not standard form. It equals 8.1 × 10⁸.
markPoints: B1 State coefficient must be 1 ≤ a < 10
M1 Shift coefficient one decimal place

questions.prompt: A pupil writes (8 × 10⁻³) ÷ (2 × 10⁻⁵) = 4 × 10⁻⁸. Explain the error and correct the answer.
questions.solution: For division subtract the exponents: −3 − (−5) = 2. The correct result is 4 × 10².
markPoints: B1 Explain exponents should be subtracted

questions.prompt: A total of 9.4 × 10⁷ particles is shared equally among 2 containers. How many particles are in one container? Give standard form.
questions.solution: Divide by 2: 9.4 × 10⁷ ÷ 2 = 4.7 × 10⁷ per container.
markPoints: M1 Divide the total by the number of containers
M1 Deal with the coefficient accurately

questions.prompt: A store contains 1.2 × 10⁸ bytes. A file occupies 4 × 10⁵ bytes. How many such files fit, assuming no other space is used?
markPoints: M1 Divide capacity by file size

questions.prompt: A total of 1.5 × 10⁹ particles is shared equally among 5 containers. How many particles are in one container? Give standard form.
questions.solution: Divide by 5: 1.5 × 10⁹ ÷ 5 = 3 × 10⁸ per container.
markPoints: M1 Divide the total by the number of containers
M1 Deal with the coefficient accurately

questions.prompt: A laboratory has 1.8 × 10⁷ cells. It uses 6 × 10⁶ cells and divides the remainder equally among 8 containers. Find the number per container in standard form.
questions.solution: Remaining cells = 1.8 × 10⁷ − 0.6 × 10⁷ = 1.2 × 10⁷. Each container receives 1.2 × 10⁷ ÷ 8 = 1.5 × 10⁶ cells.
markPoints: M1 Subtract using a common power

questions.prompt: Write 1.25 × 10^6 correct to 2 significant figures, in standard form.
questions.solution: Keep the first 2 significant digits and inspect the next digit. The coefficient rounds to 1.3; the answer is 1.3 × 10^6.
markPoints: M1 Correct rounding decision using the next digit

questions.prompt: Write 3.7548 × 10^-4 correct to 3 significant figures, in standard form.
questions.solution: Keep the first 3 significant digits and inspect the next digit. The coefficient rounds to 3.75; the answer is 3.75 × 10^-4.

questions.prompt: Write 6.25 × 10^8 correct to 2 significant figures, in standard form.
questions.solution: Keep the first 2 significant digits and inspect the next digit. The coefficient rounds to 6.3; the answer is 6.3 × 10^8.

questions.prompt: Write 8.7562 × 10^-6 correct to 3 significant figures, in standard form.
questions.solution: Keep the first 3 significant digits and inspect the next digit. The coefficient rounds to 8.76; the answer is 8.76 × 10^-6.
markPoints: M1 Correct rounding decision using the next digit

questions.prompt: A coating has 7.2 × 10² identical deposits, each of mass 2.7 × 10⁻⁶ g. Find the total mass and decide whether it exceeds 2 × 10⁻³ g.
questions.solution: There are 720 deposits. Total mass = (7.2 × 2.7) × 10^(2 − 6) = 1.944 × 10⁻³ g. This is less than 2 × 10⁻³ g.
markPoints: B1 Correct comparison with the limit

questions.prompt: A coating has 8.1 × 10² deposits, each of mass 3.2 × 10⁻⁶ g. Find the total mass in grams, then convert it to milligrams. Use 1 g = 1000 mg.
A factory produces 9.4 × 10² small components, each of mass 3.6 × 10⁻¹ g. Find the total mass in kilograms, in standard form.
markPoints: M1 Multiply mass by component count

questions.prompt: A box contains 1.2 × 10³ metal components, each of mass 4.5 g. The empty box has mass 6 × 10² g. Find the combined mass in kilograms.
questions.solution: Components: 1200 × 4.5 = 5400 g. Including the box: 5400 + 600 = 6000 g = 6 kg.
markPoints: M1 Add 600 g and convert to kg

questions.prompt: A detector reads 5.4 × 10⁻³ s, then a correction of 7.2 × 10⁻⁴ s is subtracted. Calculate the corrected time in standard form.
questions.solution: Convert the correction to 0.72 × 10^-3, then subtract coefficients. Corrected value = 4.68 × 10⁻³ s.

questions.prompt: A detector records 6.3 × 10⁻⁴ s. Subtract a correction of 8.1 × 10⁻⁵ s, then give the corrected time to 2 significant figures in standard form.
questions.solution: Corrected time = (6.3 − 0.81) × 10⁻⁴ = 5.49 × 10⁻⁴ s. To 2 s.f. this is 5.5 × 10⁻⁴ s.
markPoints: M1 Use the third significant digit 9

questions.prompt: A detector reads 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ s, then a correction of 9.4 × 10⁻⁶ s is subtracted. Calculate the corrected time in standard form.
questions.solution: Convert the correction to 0.94 × 10^-5, then subtract coefficients. Corrected value = 6.26 × 10⁻⁵ s.

questions.prompt: A device stores 8.1 × 10⁶ bytes. Each of 1.2 × 10³ files uses 6.5 × 10³ bytes. Is there enough space? Calculate the unused space in standard form.
questions.solution: Required space = (1.2 × 6.5) × 10⁶ = 7.8 × 10⁶ bytes. There is enough space; unused space = (8.1 − 7.8) × 10⁶ = 3 × 10⁵ bytes.
markPoints: M1 Multiply file count by size
B1 Enough space with valid comparison
